beginner.summary: For analysts, SQL developers and junior data engineers who know SELECT, JOIN and GROUP BY and are new to dbt. Covers the analytics engineering workflow, dbt Core with the DuckDB adapter, project structure, seeds, models, ref() and the DAG, sources and freshness, staging and mart layers, Jinja basics, materializations, generic and singular tests, documentation, node selection, Git workflow, artifacts and logs, configuration precedence, error troubleshooting, and a small shop project capstone.
prerequisites: Writes SQL with joins, aggregates, CTEs and basic window functions
Uses a terminal, Python 3 virtual environments and pip
Knows basic Git: clone, branch, commit and push, and has a GitHub account
outcomes: Install dbt Core with DuckDB, configure profiles.yml and run dbt debug successfully
Build a layered project of seeds, sources, staging models and marts connected by ref() and source()
Test, document and select parts of the DAG with generic tests, doc blocks and --select
Diagnose common compilation, database and test errors and deliver a project that runs from a clean clone

intermediate.summary: For analytics engineers and data engineers who have built a basic dbt project and now need production patterns. Covers incremental models and the microbatch strategy, snapshots, custom macros, packages such as dbt_utils, custom generic tests, unit tests, data quality strategy, dimensional modelling, Postgres and cloud warehouse differences, environments and variables, hooks and run-operation, dbt platform jobs and environments, Slim CI with defer and state, exposures and Explorer, Python models, first MetricFlow semantic models, run performance, troubleshooting and a CI-backed capstone.
prerequisites: Has built a dbt project with sources, staging models, marts and generic tests, as in the beginner level
Writes intermediate SQL: window functions, CTEs, MERGE semantics and incremental loading concepts
Uses Git branches and pull requests and can read a GitHub Actions workflow file
outcomes: Build incremental, microbatch and snapshot models that stay correct under late data, schema change and full refresh
Write macros, custom generic tests and unit tests that keep a growing project maintainable
Run the project on Postgres and in the dbt platform with environments, jobs and Slim CI using state and defer
Define first semantic models and metrics, and tune run time with threads, timing data and materialization choices

advanced.summary: For senior analytics engineers, data platform engineers and architects who run dbt at team or company scale. Covers dbt Mesh with groups, access and cross-project refs, model contracts and versions, advanced semantic layer metrics and serving, custom materializations and dispatch, advanced Jinja, the Fusion engine and migration readiness, state-aware orchestration, CI/CD gates, cost and performance engineering, observability from artifacts, security and governance, large-project architecture, legacy migration, testing at scale, platform APIs, incident response and a multi-project capstone.
prerequisites: Operates a dbt project with incremental models, snapshots, packages, unit tests and CI, as in the intermediate level
Understands warehouse cost, permissions and query profiles on at least one platform such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift or Postgres
Can write GitHub Actions or an equivalent pipeline and read dbt manifest.json and run_results.json
outcomes: Split a monolithic project into governed, versioned, contract-backed projects connected by cross-project refs
Define and serve governed metrics with the Semantic Layer and plan adoption of the Fusion engine safely
Build CI/CD, orchestration, observability and security controls that keep production dbt runs reliable and cost-aware
Lead migrations, backfills and incident response with evidence from artifacts, tests and warehouse query history
